name: ARC-AGI-3
description: An interactive agentic reasoning benchmark where agents must explore novel grid-based environments, infer goals on the fly, build world models, and adapt strategy — all without natural-language instructions. Unlike ARC-AGI-1/2, tasks are dynamic and turn-based: agents observe a 64×64 grid and issue actions across multiple levels within each environment. Performance is measured by Relative Human Action Efficiency (RHAE), comparing AI action efficiency to human baselines.
evaluation_method: RHAE (Relative Human Action Efficiency): score = (human action count / AI action count)^2 per level, capped at 1.0; later levels weighted more heavily; averaged across environments
general_score_metric: RHAE (Relative Human Action Efficiency), reported as percentage (0–100%)
typical_sota_score: <1% for frontier LLMs (e.g., Gemini 3.1 Pro 0.37%, GPT-5.4 0.26%); best non-LLM specialized agent ~12.58% as of March 2026; human baseline 100%
reputation: Launched March 2026 by ARC Prize Foundation (Francois Chollet and Mike Knoop); part of a $2M competition (ARC Prize 2026); frontier LLMs score <1% while specialized non-LLM agents reach ~12%; billed as 'the only unsaturated general agentic intelligence benchmark as of March 2026'
notes: 135 handcrafted environments at launch (25 public, 55 semi-private, 55 private), each with 6–10 progressively harder levels. Designed to prevent memorization: novel environments with no prior training exposure. Requires Core Knowledge priors only. ARC Prize 2026 requires open-source solutions (MIT/CC0). Previous ARC-AGI-1 best AI ~53.5%, ARC-AGI-2 best AI ~24% — this benchmark resets the difficulty ceiling for agentic evaluation.
